st: Put the ground fenugreek in a bowl with [[1 cup]] of the water and let it soak for 30 minutes. It will swell and turn thick and gel-like.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the lamb, the garlic and the cumin. Brown the meat on all sides for about 8 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste and green chili. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Pour in [[2 cups]] of the water, add salt, cover and simmer on low heat for 40 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the potatoes and simmer for another 15 minutes until they are soft. Keep the stew bubbling hot.
Whisk the soaked fenugreek with the remaining [[1 cup]] water and a pinch of salt for 3 minutes until it becomes a light, thick foam.
Stir the cilantro into the stew, then ladle it into a hot bowl or pot. Spoon the fenugreek froth over the top.
Serve right away with flatbread for scooping, while the stew is still bubbling under the froth.
Rinse the rice in a bowl of cool water several times until the water is clear, then soak it in fresh water for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Add the lamb, garlic, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, cumin, turmeric and [[1 tsp]] of the salt. Stir and brown the lamb for 6 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the chicken pieces and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the meat and set it on a baking tray. Strain the broth and measure [[4.5 cups]] back into the pot, keeping the spices out. Stir in the remaining [[1 tsp]] salt.
Drain the rice and add it to the broth. Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the broiler. Broil the meat for 5 minutes until the chicken skin is browned and crisp.
Let the rice rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff it with a fork and fold in the raisins if using.
Mound the rice on a big platter and lay the roasted meat on top. Serve hot.
Put the lamb in a heavy pot with [[5 cups]] of the water and a good pinch of salt. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Cover and simmer on low for 90 minutes until the meat is falling off the bone.
Lift out the lamb and shred the meat with two forks, discarding the bones and fat. Keep the broth in the pot.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, chili, cumin and coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 8 minutes until thick and saucy.
Return the shredded lamb to the broth and add the tomato mixture. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Whisk the ground fenugreek with the remaining [[1 cup]] water until it turns frothy and thick. Let it sit for 10 minutes, then whisk again.
Pour the stew into a hot, heavy bowl or pot so it keeps bubbling. Spoon the fenugreek froth on top and sprinkle with cilantro.
Serve immediately with flatbread for scooping.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl mix the flour and salt. Add the yeast mixture, [[2 eggs]] and [[0.25 cup]] of the melted butter. Stir into a soft dough.
Knead on a floured counter for 8 minutes until smooth and stretchy, then cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll each one very thin into a large round, brushing each with melted butter.
Stack the thin rounds one on top of another, folding and layering them into a pile in a buttered round baking pan. Let it rest for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Beat the remaining egg and brush it over the top, then sprinkle with the nigella seeds.
Bake for 30 minutes until deep golden brown and puffed.
Brush the hot bread with the remaining melted butter and drizzle the warmed honey over the top.
Serve warm, cut into wedges, and enjoy with more honey on the side.
Wash the cilantro well and pat it dry so the sauce does not turn watery.
Cut the stems off the chilies. Remove the seeds from some or all of them if you want a milder sauce.
Put the cilantro, chilies and garlic in a food processor.
Add the cumin, cardamom, black pepper and salt.
Pulse in short bursts until finely chopped but still a little textured.
With the machine running, pour in the olive oil and lemon juice and blend into a loose, spoonable paste.
Taste and add more salt or lemon if you like. Store in a jar in the fridge for up to a week and serve with grilled meat, eggs or flatbread.
Mix the warm water, sugar and yeast in a large bowl. Leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Whisk in the flour, salt and baking powder to make a smooth, runny batter, like thin pancake batter.
Cover the bowl and leave the batter in a warm spot for 1 hour until bubbly and doubled.
Stir the batter gently. Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and rub it lightly with oil.
Pour in about [[0.5 cup]] of batter and tilt the pan to spread it into a thin round.
Cook for about 2 minutes. Bubbles will form and burst on top. Do not flip it.
Cook until the top looks dry and spongy and the underside is pale gold, then slide it onto a plate.
Repeat with the remaining batter, oiling the pan only if it starts to stick. Serve warm with honey, eggs or stew.
Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Lower the heat. Whisk in the flour a little at a time so no lumps form.
Switch to a sturdy wooden spoon and stir hard, pressing the dough against the side of the pot, for 10 minutes.
Keep cooking until the dough is thick, smooth and pulls away from the pot.
Wet your hands, scoop the hot dough and shape it into a smooth mound on a serving bowl.
Press a hollow into the center with the back of a wet spoon.
Pour the melted butter into the hollow and drizzle the honey around it.
Serve hot. Tear off pieces and dip them in the butter and honey.
Tear the lahoh into bite-sized pieces and spread them in a wide shallow bowl or platter.
In another bowl, stir together the yogurt and milk until smooth and pourable.
Stir in the garlic, chili, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Mix in half of the cilantro.
Pour the yogurt mixture over the torn bread.
Let the bread soak for 10 minutes so it softens and absorbs the sauce.
Scatter the rest of the cilantro on top and serve cool or at room temperature.
